_authority: Local product authority under the central Builders' Doctrine (doctrine/DOCTRINE_BINDING.json). Governor-ratified meaning is FIXED; RECOMMENDED/CANDIDATE awaits or carries limited approval; OPEN is unresolved; REFUSED carries reason and reopen condition; SUPERSEDED keeps history; proof_state follows the ladder below. The orientation receipt is derived evidence, never authority.

_enforcement_vocabulary.ARMED: a real executable protection runs and has been drilled
_enforcement_vocabulary.ARMED_AS_CONFIGURED: protection is wired and drilled in-repo, but its runtime liveness cannot be proven from inside the repository (hooks)
_enforcement_vocabulary.MANUAL: human judgement with a named evidence path
_enforcement_vocabulary.UNARMED: the obligation exists and nothing yet protects it
_enforcement_vocabulary.NOT_APPLICABLE: does not apply to this product or state

product_sentence: The Gallery is a maker-led digital gallery for art and craft objects: makers present their own work with the dignity of an exhibition; visitors discover the object, understand who made it, and approach the maker directly to buy, commission or learn; payment, delivery, returns and disputes stay outside the product.
governing_line: The Gallery hosts the encounter. The maker owns the transaction.

current_product_phase.label: Architecture being settled. Doctrine bound at Stage 0; Stage 1 product and interface architecture in progress; no application source, schema, deployment or harvest exists. The H1 harvest (architecture settled) follows Stage 1 acceptance.

active_stage.label: Product and interface architecture (Build Commission v1.1 §15) — artefacts complete; awaiting the governor's review
active_stage.authorised_by: Stage 0 orientation VALID in the binding session; receipt recorded at doctrine/receipts/STAGE0-ORIENTATION-2026-09-04.md
active_stage.next_acceptance_condition: The governor reviews the Stage 1 artefacts (product/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md, product/DOMAIN_MODEL.md, ux/journeys/*, ux/INTERFACE_FOUNDATION.md, ux/reference/interface/*) and rules on the STRATEGIC open decisions in open_governor_decisions; only that ruling authorises Stage 2 (the vertical slice). Until then application source, schema and deployment configuration are not created.

stages.label: Central Doctrine assimilation
stages.gate: exact inspected Doctrine commit bound; orientation valid; guards run; drill reported honestly

stages.label: Product and interface architecture
stages.gate: the governor can see what the product is, how it moves, how the maker publishes and how the operator acts; direction accepted
stages.evidence: product/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md; product/DOMAIN_MODEL.md; product/decisions/STAGE1-GOVERNOR-DECISION-INSTRUMENT.md; product/STAGE_2_VERTICAL_SLICE.md; ux/UX_FOUNDATION.md; ux/INTERFACE_FOUNDATION.md; ux/journeys/J-001..J-004; ux/wireframes/*.png; ux/reference/interface/INTERFACE_REFERENCE_SET.md and renders/

stages.label: Closure proof

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Product thesis: The Gallery is a maker-led digital gallery for art and craft objects. Makers present their own work with the dignity of an exhibition. Visitors discover the object, understand who made it, and approach the maker directly to buy, commission or learn.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: every stage gate compares intended journey and interface against this thesis (Audit Protocol L-A24)

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Governing distinction and line: a marketplace asks how to complete the sale; a social network asks how to keep a person scrolling; The Gallery asks how to let the work be seen and make it easy to reach the person who made it. The Gallery hosts the encounter; the maker owns the transaction.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: design review lens; structural promises checked by GAL-04/GAL-08/GAL-09 loci

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Work first.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Public entrance route renders one published work at substantial scale before any feature tile; entrance render read at phone width (L-A6) plus a DOM-order assertion
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The public entrance begins with real work, not feature tiles, promotions or creator performance.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-owned presentation.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Server-side ownership rule: only the owning maker writes presentation, order, availability and retirement of their work; cross-maker denial probe under ordinary credentials
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Each maker controls the truthful presentation, order, availability and retirement of their own work.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Direct contact.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Publish gate: a gallery advertises contact only with at least one enabled public route; contact action resolves to the exact enabled route; disabled/malformed routes never render as active
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Every eligible work, commission and workshop path reaches a maker-approved external contact or registration route.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No platform transaction.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Route inventory and schema contain no cart/checkout/wallet/escrow/order/shipping/refund/dispute objects; banned-vocabulary sweep over source, schema and copy
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: No cart, checkout, wallet, escrow, order, shipping, refund or commercial-dispute workflow exists.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No transaction cut.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: No fee, commission or revenue field is linked to any sale, commission or workshop; refusal register GAL-R03; vocabulary sweep
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The Gallery receives no percentage of a private sale, commission or workshop fee.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-authored claims.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: All claim fields (work, process, price, availability, practice) are writable only by the owning maker and rendered as maker-authored; no operator or system edit of claim text
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Claims about work, process, price, availability and practice are supplied and maintained by the maker.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No quality or reliability certification.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-gate.py G5 fails any commit whose rendered copy surfaces under ux/reference/interface/surfaces/ carry the banned vocabulary; .githooks/pre-commit executes it on every commit.
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The platform does not claim that work is authentic, handmade, high quality, safe to buy, or that a maker is commercially reliable.
fixed_product_decisions.scope_debt: The sweep's root set is the rendered copy surfaces that exist today. Application source and the governed copy home enter the same root set in Stage 2; carried as obligation OBL-GAL-012 with its activation condition, never as prose inside this clause (L-A19).

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No public popularity economy.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Schema holds no public counters; no like/rating/review/comment/repost/follower-count/streak/leaderboard object or copy; vocabulary sweep
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: No public likes, ratings, reviews, follower counts, comments, reposts, streaks, leaderboards or popularity badges.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No engagement-ranked feed.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Browse ordering is a documented, deterministic function of recency, neutral rotation and explicit filters; test asserts its inputs contain no engagement signal
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Discovery is understandable and may not be driven by opaque engagement optimisation.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No paid discovery rank.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: No paid or sponsored attribute exists on any discovery input; refusal register GAL-R09
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Payment may not buy ordinary discovery position or masquerade as merit.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Public value before identity.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Anonymous probe of every public route (Browse, search, material, work, maker gallery, collection, workshop, contact handoff) returns the surface without a session
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Visitors can encounter, browse and share work without an account wall.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker email door.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Auth configuration allows email only; the complete door (create, confirm, sign in, non-enumerating denial, resend, reset, session persistence, expiry, sign out, resume, closure, suspension/reinstatement) walked on the deployed product with a real test email
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Makers create an account and sign in through email. Phone-number and social-login doors are not part of the MVP.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-led does not mean ownerless.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Operator surface with report, takedown/restore, suspend/reinstate and category management, each recorded append-only with actor, time and reason
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The platform owns reliable access, publishing, search, privacy, reporting, blocking, takedown, suspension and reinstatement.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Moderation is not curation.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Operator actions are an enumerated set (takedown, restore, suspend, reinstate, dismiss, close, category vocabulary); no ranking, featuring-by-taste or claim-editing action exists
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The operator may act on misuse, impersonation, spam and prohibited content, but does not rank or approve artistic taste.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Truth at the handoff.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The contact handoff surface renders the governed disclosure (GAL-C1) before any external navigation; test asserts by role/test-id, never literal copy
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Before leaving for direct contact, the visitor can understand that payment, delivery, returns and disputes are arranged with the maker.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No false knowledge of private commerce.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Schema records contact intent only; no sale, fulfilment or resolution status exists; copy sweep for claims of completed transactions
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The product may record contact intent, but may not claim a sale, fulfilment or resolution it cannot observe.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Opening-screen law: the first meaningful public screen opens on one real work at substantial visual scale; the visitor is already inside The Gallery. It may carry institutional identity, search, location/context, availability and navigation, but never becomes a dashboard or promotional menu that makes the work secondary.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: entrance render inspected at phone width against the approved landing reference (L-A6, L-A24); machine part shares GAL-01 locus

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Launch material vocabulary: CLAY · TEXTILE · WOOD · METAL · PAPER. These are material categories; NEW and NEARBY are browse filters, never peers in the material taxonomy. The taxonomy grows only from actual inventory and governed category decisions.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Material enum is the single configured source; the category rail renders only that enum; NEW/NEARBY live in the filter component; NEARBY is absent until location data and distance semantics exist (GAL-R14)

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Required handoff disclosure, fixed in meaning: 'You are contacting the maker directly. Payment, delivery, returns and any dispute are arranged with them; The Gallery does not process the transaction.' Wording may be refined for clarity, never in meaning; calm, readable, present at the consequential handoff, not legal theatre.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Single governed copy entry rendered by the handoff surface (shares GAL-15 locus)

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Public contact is not account identity: the maker's sign-in email never becomes public automatically; public routes are explicitly supplied and enabled by the maker; the maker sees what will be public before publishing.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Account email column is never selected into any public view or payload; payload-absence assertion under the anonymous persona; separate public_contact_routes records

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Public place information follows the same rule: city or broad locality may support discovery; an exact studio, home or workshop address appears only when the maker supplies it for that purpose; precise location is never inferred or exposed from account, device or upload metadata.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: EXIF/location metadata stripped at upload; location fields are explicit structured maker input with a public/private flag

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Authorisation proof required: anonymous reads only public published material; a maker changes only their own records; Maker A cannot read Maker B's drafts or change Maker B's profile, work, collections, workshops or contact routes; a suspended maker cannot publish or exercise maker privileges; operator authority is separate, minimal and auditable; sensitive fields are absent from unauthorised responses; server-side or data-layer controls enforce these rules; two synthetic makers exist from the first meaningful data layer.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Adversarial live probes per persona per table under ordinary credentials (Playbook Stage 6); grants probed separately from row policies

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Repository roles: Thegallery is the only writable product repository and base branch; builders-doctrine is the read-only central Doctrine authority and is never committed to, pushed to or edited from a product session.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-hook.py GUARD-1 denies any shell, file-write or GitHub-API act that targets the Doctrine checkout or repository, wired through .claude/settings.json; .githooks/pre-push refuses a push whose remote URL names builders-doctrine. Drilled by scripts/doctrine-drill.py.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: The push route is compulsory (git runs the hook); the agent routes are as-configured (the host must have loaded this project's hook configuration). The weaker of the two is the honest claim.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Fail-closed rule: until a valid current orientation receipt exists, reading, inspection and diagnosis are allowed; application source, schema and configuration mutation, deploy, release and completion claims are blocked; missing, contradictory, ambiguous, stale or unavailable authority is BLOCKED with the exact cause.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-hook.py GUARD-2 denies a consequential act when scripts/doctrine-orient.py check fails, and GUARD-0 denies when the guard cannot establish a verdict at all; .claude/settings.json wires it to every mutation-capable tool.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: In-session mutation is guarded only as-configured. The commit and push routes are held separately and compulsorily by GAL-G7.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Authority order. Product meaning: governor's latest explicit decision > product-local authoritative decisions in Thegallery after valid binding > FIXED provisions of the Build Commission > approved Concept Note > archetype research as evidence > Fable's documented recommendation. Process and proof: exact bound Doctrine commit and its verified mechanisms > product-local binding, state and executable gates > packaged snapshots only where they do not conflict.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: applied at every decision; the binding fixes which Doctrine commit is authority

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No real person's art, address, phone number or email appears in committed fixtures, screenshots or tests; synthetic makers and visitors only.
fixed_product_decisions.source: THE_GALLERY_FABLE_5_BUILD_COMMISSION_v1.1.md §15; Canon 'Screenshots for publication come from the synthetic world'
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-gate.py G5 fails any commit whose rendered surfaces carry an email outside the reserved example domains or a real-shaped phone number; .githooks/pre-commit executes it.
fixed_product_decisions.scope_debt: Committed fixtures and screenshots enter the same sweep in Stage 2 (OBL-GAL-012).

fixed_product_decisions.summary: The product name lives in exactly one machine-readable home (product_identity in this file and the binding); code and copy read it from there and former or alternate names are swept.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Name-sweep gate over source and copy once source exists

fixed_product_decisions.summary: An indeterminate guard verdict is a denial: the guard's own crash, an unparseable payload, an absent payload or a corrupt mutation-surface file may not authorise a consequential act. Read-only tools are never matched, so inspection and diagnosis survive any guard malfunction, and governance paths stay writable so the guard can be repaired.
fixed_product_decisions.source: Governor enforcement-closure instruction 2026-09-04, taken as the derogation the Canon's fail-open ruling reserves to the Governor
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-hook.py GUARD-0 exits 2 on every indeterminate path; .claude/settings.json matches only mutation-capable tools, derived from doctrine/MUTATION_SURFACE.json and held by scripts/doctrine-gate.py G2.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: The one fail-open this cannot close is structural: the host treats any non-zero exit other than 2 as a non-blocking error, so a guard that never starts (missing interpreter, missing file) lets the act through. That residue is OBL-GAL-010 and is why the compulsory git layer exists.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No commit and no push happens on an invalid, stale or absent orientation, and no commit happens while the repository gates are red.
fixed_product_decisions.source: Builders' Playbook §3 consequence gate; Governor enforcement-closure instruction 2026-09-04
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push run scripts/doctrine-orient.py check and scripts/doctrine-gate.py, and refuse the act on failure or when the interpreter is absent.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: Compulsory for every local git commit and push in this checkout, by any actor. The residue is `--no-verify`, which is deliberate and visible; the CI job named in doctrine/EXTERNAL_ENABLEMENT.md is the layer that closes it.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No commit or push reaches the default branch from a build session; the default branch is reached through review.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: .githooks/pre-commit refuses a commit on main or master and .githooks/pre-push refuses a push to refs/heads/main or refs/heads/master; scripts/doctrine-hook.py GUARD-3 denies the same acts through the shell and the GitHub API.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: Compulsory locally. A push made outside this checkout, or a merge performed in the GitHub UI, is the governor's own act and is not this product's to prevent; branch protection is the platform layer (doctrine/EXTERNAL_ENABLEMENT.md).

fixed_product_decisions.summary: The active stage's blocked list is enforced, not remembered: application source, schema and deployment configuration cannot be created while the stage blocks them.
fixed_product_decisions.source: doctrine/PRODUCT_STATE.json active_stage.blocked_until_acceptance; Commission v1.1 §15 stage gates
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-hook.py GUARD-4 denies a local write into an application root or build manifest while active_stage.blocked_until_acceptance names it.
fixed_product_decisions.layer_note: As-configured at the hook layer; the compulsory layer is that such files would have to reach a commit, where GAL-G7's gates run.

mandated_outcomes.outcome: Structural model: shared public Gallery → maker-owned gallery → individual work → maker's practice → commission or workshop invitation → direct contact handoff. The shared environment enables discovery and never displaces the maker's gallery as the place where a body of work is understood.

Visitor journey: enter without signing in; encounter work; open one work at meaningful scale; understand it through restrained factual information; move into the maker's gallery and practice; save privately, share the exact link, or choose a contact intention; see the direct-contact boundary and move to the maker's approved route. No platform checkout after contact.

Maker journey: For Makers → email account with real deployed verification → maker/studio/collective identity, location, practice note, public contact routes → gallery and first work → deliberate arrangement and optional collections → work status, commission availability, workshops → share → receive enquiries outside the platform → maintain, reorder, unpublish, retire → edit profile, recover access, sign out, close account through complete paths.

Operator journey, required before public launch and not before the first validated maker-to-visitor chain: protected door; new reports and unresolved operating failures; inspect with context; takedown/restore, suspend/reinstate, dismiss/close; record reason and outcome without rewriting history; manage the material vocabulary; identify failed publishing/contact paths.

Accessibility and professional behaviour: WCAG 2.2 AA; no low-contrast, colour-only or delicate-type dependence; active categories signalled by more than amber; labelled icons; component-level touch, focus, keyboard and screen-reader design; maker-authored alt text with an honest fallback; reduced-motion respected; every loading, empty, partial, stale, failed and denied state is a designed surface.

Technical and data integrity standard: durable deep links and truthful share previews; managed email authentication; persistent database; proper object storage with non-destructive image variants; server-side access controls; migration discipline; environment separation with no credentials in source; diagnostic logging; a deployed phone-walkable environment; no service-worker fetch cache. The twelve decisive integrity seams of §13 hold.

Professional UX completeness: the before, during, success, failure, interruption and return states of every meaningful journey are designed; the state families of §14 are represented; forms ask only for used data, explain public vs private, validate near the field, preserve input, preview before consequential publishing, prevent duplicate submission, and name consequences before destructive acts; excellent behaviour from a WhatsApp link in a mobile browser at small phone, large phone, tablet and desktop widths; observed performance, not inferred.

recommended_decisions.summary: Artist and artisan boundary without certification: maker self-declaration at gallery creation, clear participation rules, a report route for impersonation, prohibited resale or systematic misuse, operator takedown/suspension with appeal/reinstatement, and no 'verified', 'vetted', 'authentic' or 'safe' claim. No pre-publication quality or taste gate in the MVP. A stricter admission system is a governor decision.
Navigation: Browse · Saved · Workshops · For Makers, with search globally available. Fable may refine only with a shown comparison that weakens no journey (Stage 1 records the comparison).

Work commercial/display status: available · made to order · enquire · sold · on view — separate from the work lifecycle draft → published → retired; stale status is detectable and honestly labelled or prompted for reconfirmation.

Email credential flow: email plus password with email confirmation and password reset is the current recommendation; an emailed one-time code is coherent if supported well; a magic-link-only door is refused without a proven cross-device, real-mail-client round trip.

Optional paid identity confirmation is not in the MVP. If opened, it confirms only that the person or studio controlling an account matches the displayed identity; it never implies authorship of every work, quality, handmade authenticity, transaction safety or higher rank; no badge before review, privacy, renewal, appeal and revocation mechanisms exist.

Revenue direction: maker-funded presentation infrastructure (free gallery; subscription studio plan; institutional plan) — never a transaction percentage, advertising or pay-to-rank. Monetisation implementation is deferred; the presentation architecture stays subscription-ready.

Success measures: work-detail open rate; direct-contact action from eligible work or gallery; active makers with current published work; inventory freshness and status reconfirmation; return visits and private saves without public counts; workshop and commission contact intent; failed publish/contact rate; report rate and operator resolution time; first-attempt completion of the decisive maker publishing chain. Never scroll time, posts per day, reactions, follower growth or GMV.
A gallery may publish without a contact route; contact is not advertised until a route exists and Studio shows the task. GAL-03 holds because no path is offered before a route exists.
Sold and on-view works stay visible with their status; only retirement removes a work from public surfaces.
A status unconfirmed for 90 days is labelled publicly and prompts the maker to reconfirm; nothing is auto-retired.

refusal_register.refused: Cart, checkout, payment provider, wallet, escrow, order history or any in-product payment.
refusal_register.reason: The Gallery hosts the encounter; the maker owns the transaction (GAL-04). A checkout turns the platform into the merchant.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Only a governor decision that changes GAL-04 and the product's meaning; no implementation convenience reopens it.

refusal_register.refused: Platform-managed shipping, delivery tracking, returns, refunds, warranties or dispute resolution.
refusal_register.reason: The platform cannot observe or guarantee private fulfilment (GAL-04, GAL-16).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-04.

refusal_register.refused: Any percentage of a sale, commission or workshop fee; transaction-linked platform commission.
refusal_register.reason: Fixed revenue principle GAL-05: earn from presentation, not the sale.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-05.

refusal_register.refused: In-app buyer–maker chat or enquiry relay.
refusal_register.reason: Contact is a handoff to the maker's own route (GAL-03); an in-app channel makes the platform the intermediary and creates a moderation and privacy duty it does not own.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision after Stage 3 evidence that external routes fail visitors; would require a moderation and privacy design first.
refusal_register.source: THE_GALLERY_FABLE_5_BUILD_COMMISSION_v1.1.md §11 'Deliberately excluded from the MVP' and §4; THE_GALLERY_FABLE_5_BUILD_COMMISSION_v1.1.md §17 contact routes

refusal_register.refused: Managed commission proposals, contracts, deposits, milestones or delivery tracking.
refusal_register.reason: Commission availability is an invitation to enquire, not a managed job (GAL-04).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-04.

refusal_register.refused: In-app workshop ticketing or payment.
refusal_register.reason: Workshops hand off to direct contact or an external registration route (GAL-04).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-04.

refusal_register.refused: Public likes, ratings, reviews, comments, reposts, follower counts, streaks, leaderboards or popularity badges.
refusal_register.reason: No public popularity economy (GAL-08); makers must not perform for reactions.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-08.

refusal_register.refused: Personalised engagement-ranked or infinite feed.
refusal_register.reason: Discovery must be explainable (GAL-09).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-09.

refusal_register.refused: Advertising, sponsored works in ordinary discovery, paid placement or pay-to-rank.
refusal_register.reason: No paid discovery rank (GAL-10).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-10.

refusal_register.refused: Platform judgement of artistic merit, craft quality, handmade authenticity or commercial reliability, and the vocabulary verified · vetted · certified · safe · guaranteed · authentic.
refusal_register.reason: A claim creates a verification duty the platform does not perform (GAL-07, GAL-14).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Only a narrow implemented mechanism that earns the exact statement, ruled by the governor.
refusal_register.source: THE_GALLERY_FABLE_5_BUILD_COMMISSION_v1.1.md §11 'Deliberately excluded from the MVP' and §4; THE_GALLERY_FABLE_5_BUILD_COMMISSION_v1.1.md §9 copy discipline

refusal_register.refused: Identity-confirmation badge in the MVP.
refusal_register.reason: No badge before review, privacy, renewal, appeal and revocation mechanisms exist (GAL-RC5).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor reopens with an operating mechanism, price and exact narrow claim; never tied to rank.

refusal_register.refused: Phone-number and social-login doors.
refusal_register.reason: Maker email door is fixed for the MVP (GAL-12).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision after the email door is proven and evidence shows a need.

refusal_register.refused: A public sign-in wall or mandatory visitor registration.
refusal_register.reason: Public value before identity (GAL-11).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never for browsing or contact; an optional visitor account only for cross-device saves, following or notices, by governor decision.

refusal_register.refused: A Nearby filter before real location data and distance semantics exist.
refusal_register.reason: A filter must name what it does; a fake Nearby is a promise without a mechanism.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Structured maker location with public/private flag and a defined distance origin exist and are probed live.

refusal_register.refused: A service-worker fetch cache or offline app shell.
refusal_register.reason: The product reads live data on every screen; a shell cache strands stale clients (Canon, deploy & caching, superseded law).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: A deliberately designed useful offline behaviour ruled by the governor.

refusal_register.refused: Dormant UI, empty navigation or placeholders for excluded features.
refusal_register.reason: Structure makes claims by position; a tab or button promises a capability.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never; excluded features are absent, not disabled.

refusal_register.refused: Decorative or vague interface copy (e.g. 'Enter today's rooms') and manufactured artisanal mood copy (e.g. 'made slowly, altered by hand').
refusal_register.reason: Copy is an interface to mechanisms; unsupported atmosphere is a claim without an artifact.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never as platform copy; a maker's own attributed note may appear.

refusal_register.refused: A magic-link-only sign-in door without a proven real-mail-client, cross-device round trip.
refusal_register.reason: Magic links failed in the field on a prior build (Canon, identity & the door; Audit Protocol E1).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: A deployed round-trip walk on a phone with a real email proves it.

refusal_register.refused: A free-form gallery page builder, and premium presentation work before the core publishing and contact chain is reliable.
refusal_register.reason: Beauty cannot substitute for reliability at the decisive seam (research brief §3).
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Core chain proven (Stage 2 gate) and a governor decision on the 3–5 gallery modes.

refusal_register.refused: Writing to builders-doctrine from a product session; treating copied Canon/Audit snapshots or a manual read-first ritual as assimilation or binding.
refusal_register.reason: Doctrine is central; binding is local; copies are not authority.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never.

refusal_register.refused: Any real person's art, address, phone number or email in committed fixtures, screenshots or tests.
refusal_register.reason: GAL-G4; Canon publication rule.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never.

refusal_register.refused: Inferring or exposing precise location from account, device or upload metadata.
refusal_register.reason: GAL-P2 privacy rule.
refusal_register.reopen_condition: Never.

unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.summary: Host invocation of this project's hooks is unproven after two attempts, which failed on two different preconditions. Attempt 1 (2026-09-04, receipt doctrine/receipts/HOOK_LIVENESS_ATTEMPT-2026-09-04.md) tested nothing: the harness continued the session that had created .claude/settings.json rather than starting a fresh one. Attempt 2 (2026-09-06, receipt doctrine/receipts/HOOK_LIVENESS_ATTEMPT-2026-09-06.md) was a genuinely fresh session with the file tracked in the checked-out commit and on disk 1.87 seconds before the harness's first settings load, and still not one hook spawned: the harness's own diagnostics record exactly one hook spawn in the whole session, its own git-identity SessionStart hook, and zero PreToolUse spawns against 14 Bash calls and 1 Write call that the matcher covers. The cause is project-settings discovery, not snapshot timing: the session's project root was /home/user, the parent directory holding this repository and the Doctrine checkout as siblings, and the harness looks for project settings at <project root>/.claude/ only, so .claude/settings.json one level deeper was never a discovery candidate. Snapshot timing, matcher behaviour and guard logic are each ruled out by that evidence; the hook door itself works here, since a settings file at the project root did fire.

unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.activation_condition: The governor opens a session whose working directory and project root ARE this repository, not a parent that also holds the Doctrine checkout, with the Doctrine checkout supplied through DOCTRINE_ROOT; and steps 0a, 0b and 0c of doctrine/receipts/HOOK_LIVENESS_VERIFICATION.md confirm session freshness, project-root identity and the harness's own hook-spawn record before any probe runs.
unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.future_acceptance_test: The SessionStart output of that session contains the standing assessment and the line 'DOCTRINE GUARD: pre-act enforcement live for this session', the harness diagnostics record a PreToolUse hook_spawn for a covered tool call, and a deliberate reversible denial attempt in that session returns a GUARD-rule denial. unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.summary: Host-level fail-open residue: the harness treats exit code 2 as a block and every other non-zero exit as a non-blocking error. A guard that cannot start at all (interpreter absent, file removed, process killed) therefore lets the act proceed, and nothing inside the guard can prevent that. This is the reason the compulsory git layer and the CI layer exist rather than an argument that the hook layer suffices.

unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.summary: The compulsory git layer is armed by the as-configured hook layer, so the two are not independent and neither was live in the container of 2026-09-06. .githooks/pre-commit and pre-push run only when core.hooksPath names .githooks, and the single place in this repository that sets it is scripts/doctrine-hook.py line 379, inside session_start — the SessionStart hook. In a fresh clone where that hook does not fire, git config core.hooksPath is empty and the hook files are inert however fail-closed their contents are. Observed directly: a deliberate git commit --allow-empty reached the branch with no refusal from any layer, and was reset (doctrine/receipts/HOOK_LIVENESS_ATTEMPT-2026-09-06.md probe C and section 6). Gate G3 checks that the hook files exist, are executable and carry no fail-open path, all true; it does not check that git is configured to run them. README.md states 'core.hooksPath is set by the seam', which is inaccurate — scripts/doctrine-orient.py never touches it. This puts GAL-G7's ARMED classification in question. It is deliberately NOT reclassified here and armed_fixed_decisions is not moved: that is a recorded governed movement, and the session that found this was bounded to hook-liveness verification. Two candidate repairs, for the governor to choose between: arm core.hooksPath in scripts/doctrine-orient.py orient so the seam does what README already claims and the git layer stops depending on the harness; or extend gate G3 to fail when core.hooksPath does not name .githooks, so an unarmed clone is red rather than silently inert. Either needs its own drill case and its own ratchet movement.
unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.activation_condition: The governor rules on which of the two named repairs to make, or directs that GAL-G7 be reclassified to reflect that its arming depends on the harness hook layer.
unresolved_material_findings_or_obligati.future_acceptance_test: In a clone where no harness hook has run, a commit that violates the gates is refused; a drill case asserts that refusal with core.hooksPath unset at the start of the case; and doctrine/RATCHETS.json records the resulting movement of armed_fixed_decisions in the same change.
